Purpose and exclusions

Vanguard, Ranger, Arcanist and Warden share a common body but differ through authored abilities, stat growth and talent graphs. The backend validates points, prerequisites/exclusivity and respec atomically; UI lines on a tree are not rules.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Author four DA_Class_* growth/ability catalogs and four DA_SkillTree_* graphs. Start Vanguard/Ranger combat visuals in the slice when supported; Arcanist/Warden casting/healing visuals are explicit art tasks.
  2. Populate sources/class-catalog.json with six example abilities and a small three-branch talent plan per class; these are production templates, not a balanced 50-level tree.
  3. Build WBP_Skills with keyboard/controller node navigation, rank/cost/requirements, confirmation and respec preview. Use a list alternative for accessibility.
  4. Place NPC_TovinTrainer and assign trainer service plus class/profession offers. Reopen dialogue, wallet and GAS grant lifecycle for the respec result.
  5. Validate graph acyclicity, class membership, no required story gate tied to an irrevocable exclusive node, and all referenced ability/effect IDs.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Functions, commands and event bindings

Project custom contracts are not engine/plugin nodes. A read-only asset participates through its consumer; it does not inherit that consumer’s mutation methods. Backend endpoint pages label transport proposals explicitly.

ContractExecution / effect
RequestSpendSkillPoint(CommandId, NodeId, Rank, ExpectedBuildRevision) -> Purchased|PrerequisiteMissing|ExclusiveConflict|InsufficientPointsNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.
GetRespecQuote(TrainerContext) -> Quote|NoServiceNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.
ConfirmRespec(CommandId, QuoteId) -> ResetBuild|StaleQuote|InsufficientFundsNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.
ValidateSkillGraph(TreeId) -> Valid|Cycle|MissingNode|UnreachableRequiredProgressNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Four classes, talents, prerequisites and respec. Rule owner: URPGSkillComponent. This asset’s role is Vanguard, Ranger, Arcanist and Warden share a common body but differ through authored abilities, stat growth and talent graphs. The backend validates points, prerequisites/exclusivity and respec atomically; UI lines on a tree are not rules.

  1. Player opens WBP_Skills and sees eligible nodes computed from the current versioned build; locked nodes explain exact missing requirements.
  2. Spend request identifies node/rank only. Server/backend checks class, level, points, prerequisites, exclusive group and current build revision.
  3. Commit node ranks and point spend, increment build revision, and return the new durable build.
  4. Zone rebuilds GAS granted abilities/passives from the committed set, removing obsolete grants/effects without duplicating remaining ones.
  5. At trainer, respec quote specifies cost and scope; confirmation debits currency and resets the selected tree/ranks in one transaction. Restore required baseline abilities independent of optional talent choices.
  6. Reconnect/transfer reconstructs the same build from stable IDs; content migration validates removed/replaced nodes and refunds points under a recorded policy.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_Rillmere / NPC_TovinTrainer / TalentFixture_A. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Spend same points concurrently -> one valid commit; other StaleRevision/InsufficientPoints.
Skip prerequisite via forged request -> PrerequisiteMissing.
Buy both exclusive branches -> ExclusiveConflict.
Disconnect after respec charge -> one reset/charge, correct build on reconnect.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not duplicate a native rule in Blueprint, assume a planned type is compiled, or keep callbacks/owners valid after world or session replacement.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
